title: Authorization ledger cutover and backfill orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: perform a controlled migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 ensuring authorization state parity, audit log preservation, SSO/SAML mapping continuity, and safe admin control handoff. This ticket coordinates the orchestration around dual-write, incremental reconciliation (backfill), a staged cutover window, and the external customer communications required for higher-risk tenants.

Scope: dual-write shim deployment, backfill job orchestration (per-tenant, per-region), reconciliation automation (fast/slow paths), canary cutover for low-risk tenants, staged waves for production tenants, admin emergency access validation, SSO/SAML mapping verification, audit-forwarding validation, and rollback runbook. Does NOT include UI changes to console role editor (handled in DES/PM tickets).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dual-write shim enabled and verified with 1000 TPS synthetic traffic showing write parity for keys and metadata.
2) Backfill job completes for a pilot tenant (pilot verified).
3) Automated reconciliation job reduces mismatched authorization entries to <0.01% across sampled tenants.
4) Auditing: audit-forwarder captures RBAC v2 events with preserved trace IDs and faces no gaps during cutover window.
5) SSO/SAML: identity mappings for pilot tenants match expected role mappings; SSO login/role projection smoke tests pass.
6) Canary cutover for wave 1 completes with no customer-facing errors for 48h.
7) Rollback plan tested via simulated rollback on a staging wave.
8) Customer comms templates approved by Legal and Support.
9) Post-cutover monitoring dashboards and alerts live in Grafana.
implementation_plan:
Phase 0 - Prep: finalize data model alignment doc, secure KMS keys for audit-forwarder, create dual-write shim feature flag and telemetry.
Phase 1 - Dual-write deploy: deploy shim behind feature flag in canary region; run parity checks with synthetic workloads; collect telemetry.
Phase 2 - Backfill pilot: run backfill for pilot tenant (non-critical); validate reconciliation; fix edge cases (service accounts, resource renames, orphaned grants).
Phase 3 - Reconciliation automation: enable continuous reconcile workers (fast path for small diffs, slow path for large repairs) with rate limits and quota awareness.
Phase 4 - Canary cutover: execute cutover for wave 1 (10% of tenants by usage) during maintenance window; monitor for 72h.
Phase 5 - Staged waves: increase coverage by pre-defined wave sizes with intervening verification checks.
Phase 6 - Cutover completion: flip global feature flag once waves meet acceptance.
Phase 7 - Post-cutover cleanup: deprecate v1 write paths, run final reconciliation, archive v1 artifacts per compliance policy.

Each phase includes a clear rollback gating condition and a named on-call owner for 24/7 support during windows.
rollout_steps:
1) Prepare runbook and assign on-call rotations (SRE, Security, Product).
2) Launch dual-write in canary region behind feature flag; run 24h parity job.
3) Kick off backfill pilot for tenant 'pilot-redwood-1' with start/end metrics.
4) Validate audits and SSO mappings; collect stakeholder sign-off.
5) Schedule wave 1 cutover (low-risk tenants) in a 2-hour maintenance window.
6) Monitor key metrics for 72h. If stable, schedule next wave.
7) For each wave, run a preflight checklist (DB checksums, message queue backpressure, rate-limit headroom).
8) After final wave, enable global cutover and start v1 deprecation timer.
monitoring_and_mitigation:
Monitoring: track these dashboards/alerts - write-parity-rate (<0.1% mismatch), backfill-success-rate (>99%), reconciliation-lag (<5m for fast path), audit-forwarding-latency (<2s median), SSO-mapping-failures (count), error-rate (5xx) on critical auth endpoints.
Alerts: page on parity drop >0.5% sustained for 10m, backfill job failure >3 retries, audit-forwarder backlog >10000 events, SSO mapping errors spike >10x baseline.
Mitigation steps: pause new waves and open investigation; revert feature flag; rollback dual-write to v1-only; re-run reconciliation in dry-run; engage Security and SRE for audit gaps; notify customers if any tenant data inconsistency is possible.
communications:
Internal: pre-migration Slack channel #rbac-v2-cutover, daily standups during migration window, immediate incident channel during active waves.
Customer: staged email templates - (A) Heads-up 2 weeks before tenant wave, (B) Maintenance window notice 48h before, (C) Post-cutover confirmation with support contacts. Templates linked in Confluence.
Support escalation: tiered escalation matrix with named exec contact for high-severity customer impact.
Legal/Compliance: provide migration timeline and audit log retention plan prior to wave 1. Templates must be approved by Legal one week before deployment.
notes:
Trade-offs and decisions:
- Chose dual-write + backfill vs big-bang export-import to preserve live telemetry and reduce downtime risk.
- Backfill rate-limited to avoid DB hotspots; will use tenant-weighted priority for large enterprise tenants.
- Reconciliation favors idempotent repair operations; destructive fixes require explicit approval.
- Admin emergency access: maintain a short-lived bypass token for SRE during cutover; all actions logged and audited.
- We will keep RBAC v1 reads for 2 weeks post-cutover to serve any stray legacy clients, then deprecate.

Open questions: how to handle third-party integrations that call raw RBAC tables? Need inventory (owned by Solutions Engineering).
